known.title: The user choice to report every open issue with a non-null stateReason as unreadable rests on a false premise: GitHub sets stateReason to REOPENED when an issue reopens, so every reopened plan reads unreadable and can no longer move.
known.locator: Research, Decisions, entry 2 (line 53); Research, Record design, status truth table (line 43); Steps, row 1 contract_text (line 82) and row 3 cli_statuses (line 84)
known.summary: User: decision 2 reads the phase label of an open issue only while stateReason is null and reports an open issue with any stateReason as unreadable, because 'GitHub sets stateReason when it closes an issue and clears it when the issue reopens'. Official GitHub documentation contradicts the premise: the GraphQL IssueStateReason enum holds REOPENED, 'An issue that has been reopened' (https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/enums#issuestatereason, the page that the plan's Sources cite), and the REST issue object lists state_reason `reopened` (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/issues#update-an-issue). A live read on 2026-10-26 shows open issues cli/cli#11942 and cli/cli#10951 with stateReason REOPENED. Scenario: the snapshot contract says GitHub closes a plan as soon as the first pull request with a closing keyword merges (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/references/plan-contract.md:212), and reopening such a plan, or any plan closed by mistake, sets stateReason REOPENED. Under contract_text and cli_statuses that open plan reads unreadable: status has no transition from unreadable, step requires ongoing (plan.mjs:652, kept), and list shows it as broken, so the Goal that GitHub fields own the status fails for every reopened plan. Fix: derive the status of an open issue from its one phase label whatever stateReason holds (null or REOPENED), use stateReason only for closed issues, and correct decision 2, the truth table, and the Task of contract_text and cli_statuses.

known.title: Step cli_archive changes the GitHub calls that archive makes, but no Files cell lists the gh stub fixture that parses those calls, so the archive assertions and the plan CLI suite cannot pass.
known.locator: Steps, row 4 cli_archive, Files (line 85), and row 7 tests, Files (line 88); Acceptance a8, a9, a14 (lines 101, 102, 107); Research, Acceptance conventions (line 60)
known.summary: Step cli_archive makes archive pass includeClosedPrs, read the latest ClosedEvent closer and the associatedPullRequests of the closing commit, and remove phase labels with no body write. scripts/tests/plan-cli.mjs runs the helper with scripts/tests/fixtures/gh-stub/gh first on PATH (plan-cli.mjs:11, :67-69). That stub parses the GraphQL query text: it matches only `alias: closedByPullRequestsReferences(...)` selections with a regex, dies with 'graphql query selects no closedByPullRequestsReferences field' for any query without one, and answers no timelineItems or associatedPullRequests field (gh stub :139-205, :144-153). Its `issue edit` handler dies with 'issue edit requires a body or assignee change' on a label-only edit (:289-293). No Files cell lists the stub; step tests lists only plan-cli.mjs, plan-skill-phases.mjs, and selftest.mjs. Scenario: a8 and a9 are stub rows that plan-cli.mjs holds as assertions. Against the unchanged stub the closing-commit query fails or returns no closer and the label removal dies, so a8 cannot pass, a9 refuses for the wrong reason, a14 (node scripts/tests/plan-cli.mjs) fails, and step tests cannot reach its Done when. Fix: add scripts/tests/fixtures/gh-stub/gh to the Files cell of step tests, and make it answer the closing-event and associatedPullRequests query, honor includeClosedPrs, and accept a label-only issue edit.

known.title: Acceptance a7 claims to prove that the blocked reason moves to the first line of Open questions, but it only checks the existing refusal of a missing --reason, so it passes before the change and no row checks that Goal outcome.
known.summary: The Goal says that a blocked plan keeps its reason as the first line of ## Open questions, written `Blocked: <reason>`. Row a7 runs `plan.mjs status <n> blocked` without --reason and expects exit 1 with 'blocked status requires --reason as single-line text', 'which proves that the reason is written as the first Blocked: line'. At this commit setPlanStatus already refuses exactly that, before it reads the issue (plan.mjs:633), and cli_statuses keeps the refusal, so the row passes before and after the change. It never runs a blocked write with a reason, so an implementation that drops the reason or still writes a blocked_reason key also passes. No other Acceptance row checks the Blocked: line: a1 to a6 and a8 to a13 check other outcomes, and a14 to a18 are gates. Fix: make a7 run `plan.mjs status <n> blocked --reason x` on a v3 stub issue and expect ## Open questions to open with `Blocked: x` and the body to hold no blocked_reason line, then a move to ongoing that removes the line.

protected.summary: User: the user chose to keep the v2 frontmatter parser as legacy input and to convert a v2 body to v3 on its next write by the changed helper, instead of converting issues #12 and #14 in this plan; the Goal covers the records that the changed helper creates or writes. Sound: plan-lifecycle 0.5.0 shipped the v2 issue record (version 0.5.0 at plugins/plan-lifecycle/.claude-plugin/plugin.json:4, plugins/plan-lifecycle/.codex-plugin/plugin.json:3, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json:70; release commit ed0b254 follows feature commit b976562, which made the record a GitHub issue). The MARKDOWN_V2 route runs `plan.mjs check --file` on each v2 source and creates byte-preserving issues from them (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-workspace/SKILL.md:150-167). The 0.5.0 helper refuses a body without plan_contract: v2 (plan.mjs:387-389) and is the only lifecycle tool (AGENTS.md:88-89), so a converted #14 would stop this plan's own lifecycle. Keeping an old reader for released data and a live migration route has a stated reason; no instruction file at the commit forbids it, the snapshot contract asks only for a named durable fix (plan-contract.md:86), which the plan gives, and the Goal is written to match, so cli_record and skill_bodies carry it out and a3 checks it.

Request correction: Asked to delete the dead labels plan:finished and plan-scheduled from the repository; Did: the changed helper stops creating, applying, and reading both labels and the contract drops them, while the two live labels stay until a follow-up plan has released the changed helper and deletes them with its own confirmation. Sound: until that release the installed helper is 0.5.0 (all three version fields read 0.5.0, and decision 3 keeps them), its archive and retire add plan:finished (plan.mjs:811), and gh resolves each --add-label name to an ID and fails with "'<name>' not found" for a missing label (https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/v2.86.0/api/queries_repo.go LabelsToIDs, called from https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/v2.86.0/pkg/cmd/pr/shared/editable_http.go), so a deletion now breaks 0.5.0 archives in this repository, the archive of this plan included (F9). The 0.5.0 labels command also recreates both labels with --force (plan.mjs:481). A live label deletion is a non-local effect that needs its own in-session ask (plan-contract.md:229, AGENTS.md:92-97), the Goal does not require it, and Do not touch records the deferral, so no rule or Goal outcome breaks.

User: the user chose to leave the version of both plan-lifecycle manifests and of its marketplace entry at 0.5.0 and to release with `node scripts/release.mjs --plugin plan-lifecycle minor` in a follow-up plan. Sound: scripts/AGENTS.md:171 releases one plugin after the merge with that command; runGenericPluginRelease (scripts/lib/plugin-release.mjs:256) writes the Claude manifest, the Codex manifest, and the marketplace entry in one run (:293-314); scripts/lib/ci-targeting.mjs:386-391 says that the bump commit goes straight to main and the tag run gates it; the 0.5.0 release took this path (b976562 changed only the descriptions, ed0b254 moved the three versions). Re-cutting a number that the manifests already carry is the recovery path after a failed tag CI (plugin-release.mjs:283-288, :397-401). The three versions stay equal, so the lockstep rule (AGENTS.md:128) and the version checks (scripts/ci.mjs:402-404, plugins/plan-lifecycle/test/selftest.mjs:95-100) hold; the Goal needs no release, and Do not touch records the choice.
